Salary Scales

The establishment of the salaries and related allowances for staff members in the General Service and Related Categories in the United Nations common system is a complex technical exercise in which a number of different parties are involved.

The methodology is established by the International Civil Service Commission (ICSC), which is also responsible for conducting the surveys in the Headquarters duty stations (New York, Madrid, London, Montreal, Geneva, Rome, Vienna, Paris, and Kingston). For all other duty stations, the UN System Chief Executives Board for Coordination (CEB) has assigned the United Nations Secretariat the responsibility for conducting the surveys and promulgating the scales.

In view of the difference in the development of local labour markets, the ICSC has established a methodology applicable to the headquarters duty stations (except Kingston) and a methodology applicable to all other survey duty stations. With respect to those other survey duty stations, this methodology further differentiates survey duty stations based on the development of the local labour market, and the number of staff members in the General Service and Related Categories stationed in the survey duty station.

In most countries, there is one salary scale applicable to all duty stations in the country, which is established on the basis of the local labour market in the survey duty station, which is normally the duty station where the common system organizations have their local headquarters. At the moment, only in the United States (New York, Washington D.C.), France (Paris, Lyon), Italy (Rome, Milan, Brindisi), Canada (Montreal, Toronto, Ottawa) and Serbia (Belgrade, Pristina) multiple scales exist.
